name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
unique: Two million works across five thousand years, including an actual Egyptian temple, a complete Frank Lloyd Wright room and the most visited costume institute on earth.
buzz: The universal advice: pick three galleries, not the whole museum. Friday nights are lively; the rooftop garden opens in summer.

name: Tenement Museum
unique: Guided tours inside a preserved 1863 tenement at 97 Orchard Street, reconstructing the apartments of actual immigrant families who lived there.
buzz: The guided only model is praised for making history intimate; booking ahead is essential and some tours sell out weeks out.

name: Comedy Cellar
unique: A basement room in the Village where famous comics drop in unannounced to work out new material; the lineup is never printed in advance.
buzz: The two-drink minimum and cramped basement are part of the deal; reviewers say the late shows are edgier and the weekend lineups worth the wait.

name: Corning Museum of Glass
unique: The largest glass museum in the world, with a hot shop where you can make your own blown ornament or flameworked bead after walking through three thousand years of glass.
buzz: The make your own sessions sell out and are worth booking first; the museum alone is a half day. Kids can do it too.

name: Storm King Art Center
unique: Five hundred acres of Hudson Valley hillside covered in monumental sculpture, Calders, Smiths, di Suveros, with a tram for tired legs.
buzz: Visitors call it the best outdoor art experience in the country; bring a picnic and rent a bike. Summer weekends get busy.

name: Letchworth State Park
unique: A 17-mile gorge with three major waterfalls, 600-foot walls and a railroad bridge over the middle fall, the Grand Canyon of the East, without the crowds.
buzz: Locals call it the best state park in the Northeast; autumn is spectacular and the lower falls trail is steep but worth it.

name: Mohonk Mountain House
unique: A Victorian castle on a cliff above a glacial lake, with 85 miles of carriage roads, a rock scramble called the Labyrinth and a lemonade porch that has served guests since Grant.
buzz: Day passes need booking and are not cheap; the Labyrinth and Eagle Cliff are the hike, and the porch is worth a slow hour.

name: High Line
unique: An abandoned elevated freight railway turned into a mile-and-a-half garden in the air, threading between starchitect buildings and the Hudson.
buzz: Locals go at 7am or after 8pm to avoid the crush; the plantings change by season and the 10th Avenue square is the photo stop.

name: Maid of the Mist
unique: A diesel boat into the base of Horseshoe Falls, where the noise and spray erase everything else, the oldest tourist attraction in North America.
buzz: Everyone gets soaked and everyone loves it; the ponchos are a joke. Go on the first boat of the day for the least crowding.

name: Bronx Zoo
unique: 265 acres of the Bronx River valley holding Congo Gorilla Forest, a monorail over the Asian plains and a bison herd descended from the animals that started the American conservation movement.
buzz: The gorillas and tigers carry it; ride the Wild Asia monorail early and skip the indoor exhibits at midday when school groups fill them.

name: Chautauqua Institution
unique: A gated Victorian village on a lake where the nine week summer program mixes daily lectures, a symphony, a ballet and a religion hall, all within walking distance of 19th century cottages.
buzz: The gate pass and parking are the hassle; once inside people describe it as summer camp for adults and stay for the amphitheater evening.

name: Dia Beacon
unique: A 1929 Nabisco box factory converted into vast skylit galleries for Minimalist and Land Art, including a room of Serra steel and fluorescent light installations.
buzz: The building is as good as the art; reviewers recommend the free guided tour and warn that the cafe is limited. Metro-North from Grand Central.

name: Katz's Delicatessen
unique: Hand-cut pastrami on rye, a paper ticket system unchanged for decades, and the table where Harry met Sally, a secular cathedral of the Lower East Side.
buzz: The pastrami is still the benchmark; staff are famously brusque and that's part of it. Expect a line at noon and cash-only-ish chaos.

name: Kykuit
unique: The Rockefeller estate above the Hudson with a six story view, a basement full of Picasso tapestries and Chinese ceramics, and a terraced garden by William Welles Bosworth.
buzz: The art tour is worth the extra ticket over the classic house tour; the coach from the visitor center is mandatory and the whole thing runs like a museum.

name: Saratoga Race Course
customer: Racing fans, groups, families on a picnic
unique: The oldest organized sporting venue in the country, where you can bring a cooler into the grandstand apron and watch the horses come down the stretch under the same 1860s trees.
buzz: The backyard picnic area is the local move; parking is a walk, the dress code is only in the clubhouse, and Travers week is chaos.

name: The Cloisters
customer: Medieval art people, gardeners, architecture fans
unique: A museum assembled from European monasteries and cloisters on a cliff in Fort Tryon Park, with the Unicorn Tapestries and a garden of medieval plants.
buzz: The building and the view of the Hudson are half the experience; the unicorn room is the reason art people make the trip uptown.

name: Watkins Glen Gorge Trail
unique: Nineteen waterfalls in a mile and a half, with stone bridges and a tunnel cut behind Cavern Cascade, on the edge of a Finger Lakes wine town.
buzz: Steep and slippery when wet; reviewers say go early and wear real shoes. Pair it with a Seneca Lake winery afternoon.

name: Institute of Culinary Education
unique: A professional culinary school that opens its kitchens to the public for single classes in knife skills, pasta, pastry and bread, taught by chefs who work in restaurants.
buzz: The facilities are professional and the classes are efficient; you leave with technique, not just a recipe.

name: Lake Placid Olympic Sites
unique: Ride a bobsled on the 1980 track, skate the oval where Eric Heiden won five golds, and take the elevator up a ski jump that looks impossible from the top.
buzz: The bobsled ride is expensive and over in a minute, and people still call it the best adrenaline hit in the state. Book ahead.

name: Murray's Cheese
unique: A Greenwich Village cheese shop with a classroom downstairs where you taste through six cheeses and learn why the same milk makes wildly different wheels.
buzz: The instructors are opinionated in the best way and the tasting is generous; the cheese 101 class sells out.

name: Shawangunk Ridge Climbing
unique: The Gunks: a quartz conglomerate cliff line with horizontal cracks so friendly that beginners lead their first routes here, plus carriage roads and a raptor migration in fall.
buzz: Guides say it is the best place in the east to learn to trad climb; the carriage roads are the backup when the cliffs are crowded.

name: Adirondack Experience
unique: A campus museum on Blue Mountain Lake with a guideboat hall, a 19th century great camp, a logging exhibit you walk through and a working blacksmith.
buzz: The guideboat collection is the surprise and the camp buildings are the reason to give it three hours; the lake view from the porch is the rest.

name: Boldt Castle
unique: A six story granite and limestone castle on an island in the St. Lawrence, abandoned mid construction in 1904 when the builder's wife died, now reached only by boat.
buzz: The boat ride through the islands is half the trip; the upper floors were never finished and the story carries the tour.

name: Breakneck Ridge
customer: Hikers, trail runners, city day trippers
unique: A rock scramble straight up the Hudson Highlands from a train station platform, three false summits and a ridge walk with the river 900 feet below.
buzz: It is the most crowded hike in the region for a reason; go before eight, wear real shoes, and skip it when the rocks are wet.

name: Buffalo AKG Art Museum
unique: A 1905 neoclassical gallery joined to a new SANAA building of glass bridges, holding one of the best modern collections in the country and a mirrored indoor bridge over a reflecting pool.
buzz: The new building is the draw but the Clyfford Still and Rothko rooms are what artists come for; the free first Friday is when Buffalo goes.

name: Cave of the Winds
unique: A wooden walkway rebuilt every spring that takes you to within 20 feet of Bridal Veil Falls, where the wind is 70 mph and the rain is going up.
buzz: The Hurricane Deck is the whole point and the poncho is useless; go early or late to avoid the tour bus hours.

name: George Eastman Museum
customer: Photographers, film people, house tour fans
unique: The Kodak founder's 1905 mansion turned photography museum, with a working film preservation lab, a Technicolor camera and the world's oldest photography collection.
buzz: The house and the technology galleries are separate pleasures; the dryden theatre screenings are the local film school.

name: Great Camp Sagamore
unique: Vanderbilt's 27 building Adirondack camp of log and twig work on a private lake, with a bowling alley and a guideboat fleet, reachable only by a long dirt road.
buzz: The guided tour is the only way in and people describe the scale as a national park lodge; stay overnight if you can, the rooms are original.

name: Harris Hill Glider Ride
customer: First time flyers, aviation people, gift buyers
unique: A sailplane ride off the ridge that hosted the first national soaring contest in 1930, where the engine is a tow plane and the silence after release is the attraction.
buzz: Riders say the 20 minute flight feels longer and the thermal over the Chemung valley is the ride; book a week out and expect weather cancellations.

name: National Baseball Hall of Fame
unique: Three floors of plaques, gloves, jerseys and the actual record of the game, in a village that invented the Cooperstown origin myth and then built a museum around it.
buzz: Even casual fans are moved by the plaque room; induction weekend in July is a zoo but electric.

name: National Comedy Center
unique: A museum where you build a personal comedy profile at the door and the exhibits adapt to it, with Carlin's notebooks, a comedy club stage and a hologram room.
buzz: People expect a small town museum and get two hours of interactive exhibits; the adult only late nights are the local favorite.

name: New York Botanical Garden
unique: A 250 acre Olmsted plan around the Haupt conservatory, with a patch of old growth forest that was never cut and a holiday train show that runs model trains past New York landmarks built out of bark.
buzz: Regulars insist on the conservatory plus the forest trail; the orchid show in spring is the busiest week of the year and needs a timed ticket.

name: Queens Night Market
unique: Sixty countries of cooking at stall prices in Flushing Meadows Corona Park under the Unisphere, with a cap that keeps most plates at six dollars or less.
buzz: Arrive at five before the lines form; the Trinidadian doubles and Colombian arepas are repeat picks, and half the stalls still want cash.

name: Sporting Clays — Golf with a Shotgun
unique: A 14-station course through Hudson Valley woods and fields where you shoot clay targets along a walking route, scored like golf, the closest thing to a round of golf with a shotgun.
buzz: Instructors are excellent with first timers and the setting is beautiful; bring a group and make it a morning. Reservations required.

name: The Wild Center
unique: A natural history museum of the Adirondacks with an elevated walkway through the treetops, otters, and a bog you can walk into without getting wet.
buzz: The Wild Walk canopy is the reason people drive three hours; the otter tank and the forest music installation are the sleepers.

name: Walkway Over the Hudson
unique: A ruined 1889 railroad bridge rebuilt as a 1.28 mile pedestrian deck 212 feet above the Hudson, with a glass elevator down to the river trail.
buzz: Sunset is the time, the wind is constant, and the elevator on the Poughkeepsie side saves the stairs; it is fully accessible.

name: Whiteface Veterans Memorial Highway
company: New York State Olympic Regional Development Authority
unique: An eight mile road that climbs to a parking lot at 4,500 feet, where a tunnel and elevator take you the last 300 feet to a summit view of the Adirondacks and Vermont.
buzz: The elevator through the mountain is the quirk; bring a jacket, since it is 20 degrees colder up top even in July.

name: Brooklyn Brainery
unique: A tiny classroom that runs cheap one off classes on everything from pickling to lock picking to the history of the subway, taught by anyone with something to teach.
buzz: The range is the appeal and the prices are low; classes are small and sell out fast.

name: Brooklyn Glass
unique: A glassblowing studio in Gowanus where beginners make drinking glasses and vases in a two hour session, then pick them up after annealing.
buzz: The instructors are working artists and the classes are small; it is a popular date night, so book early.

name: Coney Island Cyclone
unique: A 1927 wooden coaster that still feels genuinely violent, beside a boardwalk of hot dogs, sideshows and Atlantic surf in the city's outer borough.
buzz: Coaster purists insist on a back-seat ride; the rest of Coney is scruffy and that's the appeal. The Mermaid Parade in June is the day to go.

name: House of Yes
unique: A warehouse in Bushwick putting on circus, burlesque, immersive theater and themed parties with aerialists over the crowd and a strict no phones policy.
buzz: The productions are wildly creative and the crowd dresses for it; shows sell out and the space gets packed. Check the dress code before you go.

name: Martin House
unique: The prairie house Wright built for a Buffalo businessman, restored down to the art glass, with a pergola and conservatory that run the length of the block.
buzz: Guides say the two hour tour is worth it over the one hour; the restoration is the story as much as the design.

name: Allegany State Park
unique: Sixty five thousand acres of Allegheny plateau with two lakes, a stone casino built by the CCC and trails that run to the Pennsylvania line.
buzz: The Red House and Quaker areas are the two bases; the CCC casino is the rainy day building and the fall color is the peak season.

name: Ausable Chasm
unique: A sandstone gorge cut by the Ausable River with a mile of wooden walkways on the rim, a raft float through the inner chasm and a tube run down the side.
buzz: The raft through the gorge is the thing to book; the rim walk alone is fine but the water is the point and it is cold in June.

name: City Reliquary
unique: A tiny museum of New York ephemera: subway tokens, terrazzo samples, a shrine to the 1964 World's Fair and a drawer of artifacts from demolished buildings.
buzz: It is the opposite of a blockbuster museum and that is the point; the rotating displays are made by neighbors.

name: Cornell Lab of Ornithology
unique: The research lab behind eBird and the Macaulay Library, with a viewing tower over Sapsucker Woods and a wall of screens playing recordings from every continent.
buzz: Birders call the sound lab the best free attraction in the state; the trails are flat and the tower is open year round.

name: Fire Island National Seashore
unique: A car free barrier island of boardwalk villages, a sunken forest of holly and sassafras behind the dunes, and a lighthouse at the west end.
buzz: Kismet and Ocean Beach are the busy villages, Watch Hill is the quiet one, and the deer will take your lunch if you leave it out.

name: Fort Ticonderoga
customer: Rev war people, families, history teachers
unique: The stone fort at the narrows between Lake George and Lake Champlain, taken by Ethan Allen's Green Mountain Boys and later by Burgoyne, with a garden and boat tours on the lake.
buzz: The fife and drum and the cannon demonstration run on a schedule; the hours between events are best spent on the walls and in the museum.

name: Harriman State Park
unique: Forty seven thousand acres of lakes and ridge line where Seven Lakes Drive winds past swimming beaches, a stone tower and the remains of colonial iron works.
buzz: Lake Sebago is the swim, Anthony Wayne is the easy hike, and locals guard the quieter lakes; the park is bigger than the map suggests.

name: Home of Franklin D. Roosevelt
unique: Springwood, the Hudson river house where Roosevelt was born and ran a presidency, with his desk, his ship models and the grave where he and Eleanor are buried in the rose garden.
buzz: The house tour and the library are separate tickets; the grounds and the Valkill cottage next door are the quiet part most people miss.

name: Manitoga
customer: Design people, mid century fans, gardeners
unique: Industrial designer Russel Wright's house built into a quarry and a woodland garden he planted by hand, with a moss floor and a pool that reflects the hemlocks.
buzz: The house tour is the only way in and it is limited; designers leave talking about the window that frames a single tree.

name: MoMA PS1
unique: A Romanesque revival school building in Long Island City where the raw third floor rooms and the summer courtyard music series take more risks than most Manhattan museums.
buzz: The sound installations and courtyard parties are the draw; check what is installed before going, since an empty floor is still a big walk.

name: Montauk Point Lighthouse
unique: The oldest lighthouse in the state, commissioned by Washington, at the end of a 120 mile island, with 137 steps up and a view back along the whole south shore.
buzz: The climb is tighter than people expect and the wind at the point is real; pair it with the bluffs and lunch in the harbor.

name: Morgan Library and Museum
unique: J.P. Morgan's private library, with a Gutenberg Bible, the original manuscript of A Christmas Carol and a McKim building that feels like a Renaissance study.
buzz: The East Room and the study are the rooms people remember; the rotating exhibitions pull manuscripts that rarely travel.

name: Old Westbury Gardens
unique: A Charles II style manor with 200 acres of walled garden, allee and pond, built for an heir to the Phipps steel fortune and used as a set for Gatsby and The Age of Innocence.
buzz: The walled garden peaks in late May; the house tour is short and the grounds are where people spend the afternoon.

name: Opus 40
unique: A six and a half acre bluestone sculpture built by one man over 37 years in a quarry he bought for the stone, with ramps and pools that you are allowed to walk on.
buzz: People call it the best unknown place in the Catskills; the founder fell to his death at the site and is buried under the sculpture.

name: Saratoga Performing Arts Center
unique: An amphitheater in a state park where the New York City Ballet and Philadelphia Orchestra spend the summer and the lawn seats cost less than a city parking garage.
buzz: The lawn is the experience, with people carrying in full dinners and candles; the sound is better under the shell but the atmosphere is outside.

name: Sleepy Hollow Halloween
company: Village of Sleepy Hollow / Historic Hudson Valley
unique: The churchyard, bridge and mill pond from Washington Irving's story, plus a lantern-lit cemetery tour and the Great Jack O'Lantern Blaze.
buzz: The Blaze is the crowd-pleaser; tickets sell out in September. Locals warn that traffic is the real Headless Horseman.

name: Taughannock Falls State Park
unique: A 215 foot waterfall that drops into a rock amphitheater, taller than Niagara, with a flat gorge trail that takes you to the plunge pool.
buzz: The gorge trail is easy and the rim trail is the view; in winter the falls freeze and the trail becomes a ice walk.

name: The Slipper Room
unique: A tiny burlesque and variety club on the Lower East Side with a velvet stage, a live band and acts that range from classic tease to sword swallowing.
buzz: The room is intimate and the performers are professionals; get a table early and tip well. A reliable weird night out.

name: Bethel Woods
company: Bethel Woods Center for the Arts
unique: The actual hayfield where Woodstock happened, with a museum on the slope and a modern amphitheater that still books legacy acts.
buzz: The museum gets credit for honesty about the chaos and the locals; summer concerts are relaxed and picnic-friendly.

name: Antique Boat Museum
unique: The largest collection of antique wooden runabouts in the country, in a riverside boatyard where you can row a skiff or ride in a 1930s launch.
buzz: Boat people call it a pilgrimage; the river cruise in a wooden launch is the add on worth paying for.

name: Bear Mountain State Park
unique: The wooded hill above the Hudson where the Appalachian Trail crosses a zoo of native animals, a 1920s lodge and a stone tower with a view over the river bends.
buzz: The Perkins Tower drive is the easy win, the Major Welch trail is the real hike, and the lot fills by ten on fall weekends.

name: Binghamton Carousel Circuit
unique: Six working 1920s carousels spread across the city parks, all free to ride, part of a bequest that required them to stay free forever.
buzz: Collectors come from other states to ride all six in an afternoon; the Recreation Park carousel is the biggest and the oldest.

name: Buffalo Central Terminal
unique: An art deco train station abandoned since 1979, with a 225 foot concourse, a tower you can climb and water damage that makes the tile work look like a Roman bath.
buzz: The volunteer tours are irregular and sell out; photographers call it the best interior in the city and the neighborhood around it is empty.

name: Buffalo RiverWorks Kayak Tour
unique: A paddle up the Buffalo River between grain elevators the size of cathedrals, through the canal terminus where the Erie Canal met the lake.
buzz: The scale of the silos from water level is what people talk about; the water is flat and the tour is beginner friendly.

name: Culinary Institute of America
customer: Food people, couples, parents visiting students
unique: Four student run restaurants where the people cooking your lunch are weeks away from graduating, on a campus that was a Jesuit seminary above the Hudson.
buzz: Reservations are essential for the American Bounty and Bocuse rooms; the prix fixe lunch is the bargain and the bread basket is famous.

name: Grand Central Terminal
unique: A Beaux Arts cathedral of transit with a painted zodiac ceiling, a whispering gallery and a hidden platform once used for presidents.
buzz: The Oyster Bar and the whispering arch are the easy stops; the official tour gets you into the Vanderbilt room and the catwalks.

name: Griffis Sculpture Park
unique: Four hundred acres of hillside where a sculptor planted 250 steel figures among the trees, including a field of giant heads you can walk between.
buzz: People call it the strangest free art walk in the state; wear boots, since the trails are mown grass and the hills are real.

name: Harriet Tubman Home
customer: History people, students, civil rights pilgrims
unique: The brick house Tubman bought from William Seward, the home for aged people she ran next door, and the African Methodist Episcopal Zion church where her funeral was held.
buzz: The ranger tour ties the property to the underground railroad and her later life; the church across town is a separate stop on the same story.

name: Louis Armstrong House Museum
customer: Jazz fans, history people, design lovers
unique: The modest Corona house where Armstrong lived for 28 years, kept as he left it, with his reel to reel tapes and the mirrored bathroom he built himself.
buzz: Visitors are surprised it is a row house on a working block; the guided tour is the only way in and the summer garden concerts are the local secret.

name: Prospect Mountain Veterans Memorial Highway
unique: A five and a half mile road up a 2,030 foot peak with three pull offs, ending in a view of Lake George and the Adirondack high peaks on one side and Vermont on the other.
buzz: Sunset is the time and the road closes at dusk; the shuttle from the village in summer is easier than parking at the top.

name: Sagamore Hill
unique: Theodore Roosevelt's shingle style house full of trophies, books and the rocking chair where he took calls, above a cove on Cold Spring Harbor.
buzz: The ranger led house tour is the only way inside and sells out; the trail down to the beach is short and usually empty.

name: Sonnenberg Gardens and Mansion
unique: A Victorian mansion with nine formal gardens built for a banker and his wife, including a Japanese garden, a rock garden and a 1903 greenhouse range still in use.
buzz: The Japanese garden and the greenhouse are the highlights; the mansion is partly unrestored, which regulars prefer.

name: Staten Island Ferry
unique: The last free big boat ride in the country, passing the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island with a beer and a hot dog cheaper than any museum ticket.
buzz: Stand on the right going out and the left coming back; if you are short of time, ride over and take the subway back from St George.

name: Stony Brook State Park
unique: A gorge of three waterfalls and stone stairs cut into the cliff, with a swimming area at the bottom and a trail that climbs beside the falls.
buzz: The gorge trail is closed in ice season; in summer the creek pools are the swimming and the stairs get slick.

name: Untermyer Gardens
unique: A walled Persian garden and a rock and water feature built for a Gilded Age lawyer, largely forgotten for decades and now restored above the Hudson in Yonkers.
buzz: The walled garden is the reveal, and the view down to the Palisades is the second one; volunteers run free weekend tours.

name: Arthur Avenue Retail Market
customer: Food people, Italian American families, curious eaters
unique: The indoor market where Bronx Italian families still buy pasta by the pound, cigars are rolled in the back room and mozzarella is pulled in front of you.
buzz: Go on a weekday morning when the butchers are talking; Sunday after church is a crush and half the stalls are shut by three.

name: Museum of the Moving Image
unique: The only museum where you can dub a scene, play a working 1970s arcade and see the actual Muppets, all in a converted Astoria studio.
buzz: The Henson exhibition is what people come for and the arcade buys another hour; the weekend screenings are quietly excellent.

name: Blue Mountain Lake Paddle
unique: A deep clear lake under Blue Mountain with islands to land on, loon calls at dusk and a state campground on the shore.
buzz: The lake is quiet before nine and the wind picks up at noon; the islands are public and the mountain trail starts across the road.

name: Boscobel House and Gardens
customer: House tour people, gardeners, theater goers
unique: A Federal mansion moved brick by brick in the 1950s to a bluff above the Hudson, with period furniture and a rose garden that faces West Point across the river.
buzz: The view from the lawn is the best on the Hudson; the summer Shakespeare festival on the grounds is the local tradition.

name: Fort William Henry
unique: A rebuilt French and Indian War fort at the head of Lake George with musket and cannon firing, a stockade you can walk and a museum on the massacre that Cooper turned into a novel.
buzz: The live firing schedule is what children remember; the tour guides are in period dress and the lake view from the ramparts is the postcard.

name: Ganesh Temple Canteen
company: Hindu Temple Society of North America
customer: South Asian families, students, cheap eat hunters
unique: The basement cafeteria of the first traditional Hindu temple in the country, where dosas and idli are cooked to order for a few dollars and lunch is part of the visit.
buzz: The line moves fast, the ghee dosa is the standing order, and the kitchen closes for a stretch in mid afternoon.

name: Jones Beach State Park
unique: Robert Moses built six miles of ocean beach with a brick water tower and a boardwalk designed to feel like an ocean liner, and it still works as a day out.
buzz: Arrive early in summer or the lots close; the west end is quieter, the east bathhouse has the food, and the boardwalk is flat enough for anyone.

name: Motorcyclepedia Museum
unique: Eighty five thousand square feet of motorcycles including a wall of police bikes, a circular room of Indians and a 1908 Harley, put together by a collector who never sold one.
buzz: People arrive expecting a small collection and stay three hours; the police motorcycle room is the surprise.

name: New York State Festival of Balloons
unique: A small town balloon festival where 40 balloons launch at dawn and dusk from a field above the Genesee valley, with a night glow and no gate fee.
buzz: The 6am launch is the one and the wind decides everything; bring a blanket, coffee and patience, and expect to park in a farm field.

name: New York State Museum
customer: Families, history people, rainy day crowds
unique: A free state museum with a mastodon pulled from a Orange County bog, a full sized Adirondack lean to, and the largest collection of World Trade Center artifacts in the country.
buzz: The September 11 gallery is the reason many people come; the carousel and the mineral room keep children moving.

name: Noguchi Museum
customer: Design people, art students, quiet seekers
unique: A quiet block of Long Island City where Noguchi turned a photo studio and a gas station into ten rooms of carved stone, paper light and a gravel garden he laid out himself.
buzz: People call it the most calming hour in the city; the garden café is worth staying for and the shop sells small editions of his lamps.

name: Northeast Classic Car Museum
unique: A former lumber warehouse holding 160 cars from a 1908 Cadillac to muscle cars, arranged in period scenes with mannequins and garage signs.
buzz: Car people call it one of the best small collections in the east; the cars run and the volunteers will start one for you.

name: Old Fort Niagara
unique: The oldest continuously occupied military site in North America, with a French castle from 1726, earthworks above Lake Ontario and a view of the Toronto skyline on a clear day.
buzz: The castle is small and the walls are the walk; the summer French and Indian War encampment is the day to come.

name: Playland Park
customer: Coaster people, families, art deco fans
unique: The oldest continuously operating amusement park in the country, an art deco seaside complex where the 1929 Dragon Coaster still runs through a wooden dragon mouth.
buzz: Coaster people come for the Dragon and the historical buildings; the ride lineup is small and the westchester beach next door is the calm alternative.

name: Rochester Public Market
unique: A shed market that has run since 1905, with butchers, a spice stall, Jamaican patties and a Saturday morning crowd that is the most mixed room in the city.
buzz: Go Saturday before ten; the garbage plate stand across the street is the other half of the ritual.

name: Russ and Daughters
unique: A Lower East Side appetizing shop that has smoked its own salmon since 1914, with a counter of herring and a bagel sandwich that is the neighborhood's standard.
buzz: The line moves and the ordering system confuses first timers; get a number, order the super heebster and eat it on the street.

name: Saratoga Spa Mineral Springs
unique: A state park built around mineral springs where you can fill a bottle at a pavilion with water that tastes of iron and eggs, then take a carbonated bath in the 1935 Roosevelt Baths.
buzz: The taste is the story and everybody warns you; the Roosevelt Baths need booking and the park pools are the family alternative.

name: Snug Harbor Cultural Center
unique: A Greek revival retirement home for sailors turned 83 acre campus, with a Chinese scholar's garden, a botanic garden and a working lighthouse at the edge.
buzz: The Chinese garden is the surprise that brings locals back; the campus is larger than visitors expect, so pick two buildings and walk the rest.

name: Susan B. Anthony House
unique: The brick row house where Anthony ran the suffrage campaign and was arrested for voting, with the parlor where she kept the movement's books and the desk she worked at.
buzz: The guides carry the story and the basement kitchen is the surprise; it is a small house and the tour is under an hour.

name: USS Slater
unique: The last destroyer escort still afloat, a 1944 ship built in Tampa that crossed the Atlantic and now sits in the Port of Albany with its guns, depth charges and crew quarters intact.
buzz: The volunteer guides are frequently former navy and will talk for an hour; the ship is tight and steep and not for strollers.

name: Yankee Stadium Tour
customer: Baseball fans, families, visiting sports crowds
unique: The dugout, the press box and Monument Park in one walk, with a guide who has usually worked in the building since the old stadium came down.
buzz: Fans rate the guide stories above the memorabilia; weekend tours sell out and the field is off limits on game days.

name: Hook Mountain
unique: A short climb to a traprock ridge above the Tappan Zee where turkey vultures ride the updraft and the Palisades sit across the water like a wall.
buzz: The loop from Rockland Lake is the standard route; the ridge is narrow with real drop offs and the parking lot is tiny on weekends.

name: CMAC Summer Concert
unique: An open air amphitheater on the Canandaigua lakefront where the lawn slopes toward the stage and the sunset happens behind the audience.
buzz: The lawn is the value and the wine from the region is allowed in; the covered seats are for rain and the parking lot takes an hour to clear.

name: Cradle of Aviation Museum
customer: Aviation people, families, rainy day crowds
unique: Hangars of Grumman fighters, a Lunar Module and the radar dome from Mitchell Field, telling how Long Island plants built the planes that won the Pacific.
buzz: Aviation people call it underrated; the cockpit exhibits and planetarium make it the reliable rainy day backup for families.

name: Ellicottville and Holiday Valley
unique: A one street village of bars and gear shops below a ski hill that runs 750 vertical feet, with a summer jazz festival and mountain coaster.
buzz: Buffalo and Toronto both claim it in winter; the bars on Washington Street are the apres scene and the mountain is beginner friendly.

name: Erie Canal Museum
unique: A museum inside the 1850 weighlock building where canal boats were weighed, with a full canal boat cabin, the original locks and a room on the engineering that made New York the Empire State.
buzz: The building is the exhibit and the weighlock is the only one left; the upstairs gallery on the canal's labor history is what surprises people.

name: F.X. Matt Brewing Tour
unique: A fourth generation family brewery in a brick complex where you walk past open fermentation tanks and end in the 1888 tavern for samples of Saranac and Utica Club.
buzz: The tour is short but the tasting room and the old brewery architecture carry it; book ahead for Saturdays.

name: Iroquois National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Ten thousand acres of marsh and hardwood between Lake Ontario and the Niagara escarpment, with an eagle nest, a driving loop and spring migration that fills the trees.
buzz: Birders time it for the first week of May; the observation deck at Cayuga Pool is where the photographers set up at dawn.

name: Mark Twain Study
unique: The octagonal study where Twain wrote most of Huckleberry Finn, moved from his sister in law's hilltop farm to the Elmira College campus and kept as he left it.
buzz: It is a small wooden room and the visit is short, which is the point; the campus also has his grave in Woodlawn Cemetery nearby.

name: McSorley's Old Ale House
unique: The oldest continuously operating tavern in the city, with sawdust on the floor, two beers on offer and a room that has not changed since the last century.
buzz: Order the ale and skip the menu; it is crowded and cash only and the history is the point.

name: National Soaring Museum
unique: The country's hang glider and sailplane archive on Harris Hill, with 50 gliders overhead and a workshop where you can watch a wooden wing being rebuilt.
buzz: Small but serious; combine it with a glider ride next door and the day makes sense.

name: New World Mall Food Court
customer: Food crawlers, Flushing regulars, translators in training
unique: A basement food court in downtown Flushing with thirty stalls of Sichuan, Xi'an and northern Chinese cooking, most plates under twelve dollars and almost nothing translated.
buzz: Hand pulled noodles and cumin lamb skewers are the standards; go hungry, carry cash and a translation app, and avoid Saturday noon.

name: New York State Capitol Tour
company: New York State Office of General Services
customer: Architecture people, school groups, statehouse collectors
unique: A capitol built over 32 years without a dome, with a carved stone staircase that climbs four floors without support and a hall of governors that looks like a cathedral.
buzz: The Million Dollar Staircase is the thing to see; tours are free and run on the hour, and the observation deck is open in summer.

name: Parrish Art Museum
unique: Herzog and de Meuron's long barn of a building on the Water Mill fields, showing the painters who worked the light of the South Fork from Chase to today.
buzz: The building and the studio visits carry it; locals go Friday nights when admission is free and the galleries are quiet.

name: Rockaway Beach Surf Lesson
unique: The only city beach where surfing is legal, with a forgiving summer beach break and a subway station two blocks from the sand.
buzz: Beginners say the whitewater is gentler than expected and the lesson plus board package is the cheapest way into the water from New York.

name: Seward House Museum
customer: History people, house tour fans, students
unique: The Auburn home of Lincoln's secretary of state, with the desk where he wrote the Alaska purchase, a hidden staircase and a collection of Civil War flags.
buzz: The guided tour is the only way through and the guides know the Alaska story cold; the garden and the carriage house are included.

name: Six Nations Iroquois Cultural Center
unique: A small museum in the Adirondack woods with a reconstructed longhouse, dugout canoes, beadwork and a collection put together by a Mohawk family over three generations.
buzz: Visitors are surprised by the quality of the collection and the personal tour; it is off the main road and worth the detour.

name: Ska nonh Great Law of Peace Center
unique: A center on the shore of Onondaga Lake interpreting the Haudenosaunee confederacy and the Great Law, on the site of a French mission and a salt works.
buzz: The lake itself is the point, since it was sacred ground and later the most polluted lake in the country; the exhibits are small and the guides carry it.

name: The Strand Bookstore
unique: Eighteen miles of books in a 1930s building at Broadway and 12th, with a rare book room on the third floor and dollar carts on the sidewalk.
buzz: Book people call the rare room a museum and the crowds are part of the experience; go on a weekday morning.

name: Troy Waterfront Farmers Market
unique: A year round Saturday market under a brick riverside canopy where upstate farms sell cheese, cider and mushrooms and the knife sharpener works the crowd.
buzz: Locals say it is the best market in the capital region; get there by nine for the bread and stay for lunch from a stand.

name: Woodlawn Cemetery
customer: History walkers, architecture people, jazz fans
unique: 400 acres of marble and granite where Duke Ellington, Herman Melville and Miles Davis lie under mausoleums designed by McKim, Mead and White.
buzz: The weekend trolley tour is the easy way in; the gate map is good enough to walk to Ellington and Melville yourself.

name: Batavia Downs
unique: A half mile harness track where the horses come straight at you down the stretch and a two dollar bet lasts a whole evening.
buzz: Locals bring folding chairs to the apron and explain the betting to newcomers; the casino inside is louder than the track.

name: Canandaigua Lake Paddle
unique: A clear glacial lake below the Bristol Hills with a city beach at one end and a shoreline of docks, cottages and a few protected coves.
buzz: Morning is flat and empty and the lake gets choppy by afternoon; rentals are at the north end and the state park launch is quieter.

name: City Island Seafood Crawl
customer: Seafood people, boat watchers, city escapees
unique: A Long Island Sound fishing village inside the city limits: one avenue of clam shacks, boatyards and a small nautical museum, reached by a city bus.
buzz: Locals argue over which fried clam wins; the point is to walk the length of City Island Avenue and eat at two or three counters.

name: Cuba Cheese Shoppe
unique: A cheese shop in the town that supplied New York's cheese market for a century, with a cut to order counter, cheese curds and a viewing window into the plant.
buzz: The curds are the reason people detour and they sell out by afternoon; the shop is small and the sandwich counter is the local lunch.

name: Dinosaur Bar-B-Que
unique: The original Syracuse barbecue joint, started as a motorcycle gang's fundraiser and now a brick riverside hall with a blues stage and brisket that people drive from Albany for.
buzz: Expect a wait on weekends and order the ribs and the salt potatoes; the live music is loud and the room is louder.

name: Edward Hopper House
unique: The clapboard house where Hopper was born and painted the light he spent his life chasing, with his easel and a garden that faces the same south light.
buzz: Small and personal, and the reason to come is seeing the rooms that appear in the paintings; the upstairs gallery shows young artists.

name: Fort Stanwix National Monument
customer: History families, rev war people, school groups
unique: A rebuilt timber fort in the middle of downtown Rome where the 1777 siege turned back the British and where the treaty that opened the west was signed.
buzz: The rangers fire the cannon in summer and the earthworks walk is short; the museum does a good job on the Oneida alliance.

name: Historic Richmond Town
customer: Families, school groups, local history people
unique: Thirty original buildings around the old county seat, with trade shops where a tinsmith and a carpenter work in front of you on weekends.
buzz: Living history weekends are the time to go; on a quiet weekday half the buildings are locked and the visit is over in an hour.

name: Hudson River Maritime Museum
unique: A waterfront museum with a 1890s wooden tug, a working boat shop and the story of the ice harvest and brick barges that built the river economy.
buzz: Small and well made, and the lighthouse cruise and the tug are the reasons to check the schedule before driving over.

name: Jacques Marchais Museum of Tibetan Art
unique: A stone temple built into a Staten Island hillside by a self taught collector, with a terrace pond that looks lifted out of Ladakh.
buzz: Small, strange and peaceful; the terrace view is what people remember and several of the bronzes are genuinely old.

name: Long Island Aquarium
unique: A river otter and penguin operation on the Peconic with a shark tank you can snorkel and a butterfly room, small enough to finish before the children wear out.
buzz: The ray touch tank and penguin encounter are the hits; the shark snorkel is the splurge and books weeks ahead in summer.

name: Lower Falls of the Genesee
unique: A 110 foot waterfall inside the city where the Genesee cuts a gorge through 400 million year old rock, reached by a path from Maplewood Park.
buzz: Locals treat it as a secret and warn about the unofficial trails; the official overlook is a five minute walk from the lot.

name: Lucille Ball Desi Arnaz Museum
customer: TV people, families, I Love Lucy fans
unique: Lucille Ball's hometown museum with the actual Ricardo living room set, her costumes and a recreation of the chocolate factory wrapping line.
buzz: Fans love the costumes and the set; non fans are done in an hour, and the comedy center next door is the better value.

name: Merry-Go-Round Playhouse
unique: A professional musical theater in a 1930s carousel building in a state park, where Broadway actors do summer stock beside a lake.
buzz: Locals say the productions are better than a small city deserves; bring a picnic and arrive early for the park.

name: Moosewood Restaurant
unique: The worker owned vegetarian restaurant that produced the best selling cookbook of its kind, still in a converted downtown Ithaca building with a menu that changes daily.
buzz: People arrive expecting a legend and get a busy casual room; the soups and the daily specials are the order, and the cookbook shelf is by the door.

name: Oakwood Cemetery
unique: A Victorian rural cemetery on a bluff above the Hudson holding Samuel Wilson, the meat packer behind Uncle Sam, along with Civil War generals and Tiffany windows in the chapel.
buzz: The Uncle Sam grave is the photo everyone takes; the self guided map at the gate points to the Earl Chapel, which is the real monument.

name: Sackets Harbor Battlefield
unique: The naval base that kept the American fleet on Lake Ontario during the War of 1812, with earthworks, a navy yard and a view across the harbor to the Canadian shore.
buzz: The hilltop earthworks are the walk; the reconstructed barracks and the summer reenactment are the reason to check the calendar.

name: Saranac Laboratory Museum
customer: Science people, history walkers, TB families
unique: The first laboratory in the country built for tuberculosis research, where the cure was studied and where the village of cure cottages outside grew up around it.
buzz: The docents tell the story of the patients who came for the air; the lab is small and the walking tour of the cure cottages is the better half.

name: Vanderbilt Museum and Planetarium
unique: A Spanish revival mansion on a Centerport bluff holding William Vanderbilt's natural history trophies and marine collection, plus a planetarium in the old garage court.
buzz: The house is odd and personal in a way that sticks; planetarium shows are cheap and sunset over Northport Bay is why people linger.

name: Alice Austen House
unique: The 17th century farmhouse where a Victorian photographer documented immigrant New York, now a museum of her glass plates with a lawn over the Narrows.
buzz: Photographers come for the archive and stay for the porch; it is a 20 minute walk from the ferry and pairs with the waterfront path.

name: Angelica Village
unique: A Genesee valley village of Greek revival and Italianate houses around a park with a civil war monument, largely unchanged since the 1830s and used as a film location.
buzz: Architecture people call it a time capsule; the antique shops and the inn make it a half day, and the drive through the valley is the point.

name: Brotherhood Winery
unique: The oldest continuously operating winery in the country, with tours through brick cellars dug by hand in the 1830s and a tasting room in the old press house.
buzz: The cellar tour is the reason to go; the wine is not why oenophiles come back and the holiday events fill the place.

name: Conesus Lake
unique: The westernmost Finger Lake, ringed by cottages and a state park beach, with a July 3 ring of fire where every dock lights a flare at once.
buzz: The ring of fire is the local event of the year and the lake is packed that night; the rest of the summer it is quiet on weekdays.

name: Point Au Roche State Park
unique: A peninsula of Lake Champlain shoreline with a shallow sand beach, a paved bike loop and a wetland boardwalk where the lake narrows toward Vermont.
buzz: Locals call it the quiet alternative to the city beach; the lake is shallow and warm by August and the bike path is flat.

name: Roberson Museum and Science Center
customer: Families, local history people, planetarium fans
unique: A 1904 mansion with a planetarium bolted on, holding a model railroad of the region, a natural history hall and the only public telescope in the area.
buzz: The holiday model train show is the local tradition; the rest of the year the mansion rooms and the planetarium are the draw.

name: Rogers Environmental Education Center
unique: A wildlife education center on the Chenango River with a trout pond, a bird observation room and trails through old growth hemlock.
buzz: The bird feeders outside the window are the attraction in winter; it is free and the trails are flat enough for small children.

name: Splish Splash
unique: A 96 acre water park in the Pine Barrens with a half pipe slide, a lazy river and enough shade that a Long Island August afternoon is survivable.
buzz: Go on a weekday and split a cabana if you have a group; lockers and tube lines are the standard complaint in July.

name: Big Duck
unique: A duck shaped shop built by a Riverhead duck farmer to sell Peking ducks, now a landmark with a small museum inside and a holiday light show in December.
buzz: A ten minute stop that everybody photographs; the shop inside still sells decades old duck memorabilia.

name: Bowman Lake State Park
unique: A spring fed lake in the hills with a sandy beach, a campground under tall pines and a nine hole disc golf course in the woods.
buzz: Locals come for the beach in July and the quiet in September; the lake is small and the hike around it takes an hour.

name: Holland Land Office Museum
unique: The stone land office where the Holland Land Company sold off western New York by the acre, with the survey maps and the strongbox that made Batavia the capital of the frontier.
buzz: Genealogists come for the deed records and find the building itself is the exhibit; it is small and staffed by volunteers.

name: Palmer Opera House
customer: Theater people, local music fans, history buffs
unique: A restored 1903 opera house on the second floor of a main street block, with painted backdrops, wooden benches and a season of community theater and touring bands.
buzz: The room itself is the attraction and the acoustics are better than the seats; check the calendar before driving, it is not open daily.
